quote.translation: Émile Meyerson likewise points out that the law of ground is based on the law of identity: "This conviction of rationality, this conviction of necessary connection, has its origin solely in the reduction to the identity that exists between antecedent and consequent" (Émile Meyerson, Du cheminement de la Pensée, I. 1931, p. 55).

regions.text: （EmileMeyerson,DucheminementdelaPensee,1.1931,p55）～云つてゐる。理由と蹄結とは以上の如き意味に於て同一性を有してるる。

quote.translation: It follows that ground and consequent possess identity in the sense just described, and the relation between them is consequently necessary.

regions.text: 従つて雨者の開係は必然的である。それに反して理由蹄結の開係に立つてるないものは偶然的のものである。

quote.translation: Whatever does not stand in a relation of ground and consequent is, by contrast, contingent, and we can call this contingency of ground, as opposed to necessity of ground.

regions.text: それを理由的必然に對する理由約偶然といふことが出來る。きうして、後に説くところの即脚偶然と取脚知偶然とこの趣師偶然とを穂稱して假説的偶然といふ。

quote.translation: This contingency of ground, together with causal contingency and teleological contingency, which I explain later, I call by the general name of hypothetical contingency.

regions.text: 假說的偶然をこの三つに區別するのは、假說的湖係を理由性、因果性、目的性の三つに羅別することにもとづいてゐる。

quote.translation: The division of hypothetical contingency into these three rests on a division of the hypothetical relation into three, namely groundedness, causality and purposiveness.

quote.translation: Schopenhauer divided the law of sufficient reason into four roots: the "principle of the sufficient reason of becoming" (principium rationis sufficientis fiendi), the "principle of the sufficient reason of knowing" (principium rationis sufficientis cognoscendi), the "principle of the sufficient reason of existence" (principium rationis sufficientis essendi) and the "principle of the sufficient reason of acting" (principium rationis sufficientis agendi).

regions.text: sendiy「行嬌の充足理由の原理」（principiumrationissufficicntisagendi）の四つである。成の充足理由の原理とは我々の後に取扱ふ因果性に営り、認識の充足理由の原理とはいま遠べた理由性に當ら行為の充足理由の原理とは後に遠べる目的性にほぼ當つてゐる。

quote.translation: The principle of the sufficient reason of becoming corresponds to causality, which we shall treat later; the principle of the sufficient reason of knowing corresponds to the groundedness just described; and the principle of the sufficient reason of acting corresponds roughly to purposiveness, which I discuss later.

regions.text: 存在の充足理由の原理と云つてあるのは直親的存在の理由すなはち数學約理

quote.translation: What he calls the principle of the sufficient reason of existence refers to the ground of intuitive existence, that is, it is a principle concerning mathematical ground (Schopenhauer, Über die vierfache Wurzel des Satzes vom zureichenden Grunde).
